title: Ordered telescoping homotopy and annihilation on proper color supports
statement:
Let $r\geq1$, put $I=\{0,\ldots,r-1\}$, and let $(A_q)_{q\in\mathbf Z}$ be abelian groups, regarded as $\mathbf Z$-modules with the chain-complex convention of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$ and $i\in I$, let $d_q:A_q\to A_{q-1}$, $c_{i,q}:A_q\to A_{q+1}$ and $R_{i,q}:A_q\to A_q$ be homomorphisms satisfying
$$d_{q-1}d_q=0,\qquad d_{q+1}c_{i,q}+c_{i,q-1}d_q=\operatorname{id}_{A_q}-R_{i,q}.$$
Define $P_{0,q}=\operatorname{id}_{A_q}$, $P_{i+1,q}=P_{i,q}\circ R_{i,q}$ for $0\leq i<r$, and
$$H_q=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}P_{i,q+1}\circ c_{i,q}.$$
Composition always applies the rightmost map first; no commutation of different $R_i$ is assumed. Then, for all $q$ and $0\leq i<r$, $d_qR_{i,q}=R_{i,q-1}d_q$; for all $0\leq i\leq r$, $d_qP_{i,q}=P_{i,q-1}d_q$; and
$$d_{q+1}H_q+H_{q-1}d_q=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(P_{i,q}-P_{i+1,q})=\operatorname{id}_{A_q}-P_{r,q}.$$
In addition, fix any degree $q$ and suppose that for every proper subset $C\subsetneq I$ there is a subgroup $A_{q,C}\subseteq A_q$, that every element of $A_q$ is a finite sum of elements belonging to these subgroups, that $R_{i,q}(A_{q,C})\subseteq A_{q,C}$ for all $i,C$, and that $R_{i,q}$ vanishes on $A_{q,C}$ whenever $i\notin C$. Then $P_{r,q}=0$.

proof.text:
Fix $i,q$. The chain convention is that of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Solve the assumed local identity for $R_{i,q}$ and use the identity in degree $q-1$ as well. Distributing composition and using $d^2=0$ gives
$$d_qR_{i,q}=d_q-d_qd_{q+1}c_{i,q}-d_qc_{i,q-1}d_q=d_q-d_qc_{i,q-1}d_q,$$
$$R_{i,q-1}d_q=d_q-d_qc_{i,q-1}d_q-c_{i,q-2}d_{q-1}d_q=d_q-d_qc_{i,q-1}d_q.$$
Thus $d_qR_{i,q}=R_{i,q-1}d_q$ in every integer degree.

proof.text:
Induct on the prefix length $i$, simultaneously for every degree $q$. For $i=0$, both $d_qP_{0,q}$ and $P_{0,q-1}d_q$ equal $d_q$. If the equality holds at $i$, step 1 and associativity give
$$d_qP_{i+1,q}=d_qP_{i,q}R_{i,q}=P_{i,q-1}d_qR_{i,q}=P_{i,q-1}R_{i,q-1}d_q=P_{i+1,q-1}d_q.$$
This proves the prefix commutation formula for $0\leq i\leq r$.

proof.text:
Distribute $d$ over the finite sum defining $H$. For each $i<r$, step 2 in degree $q+1$ and the assumed local identity in degree $q$ give
$$d_{q+1}P_{i,q+1}c_{i,q}+P_{i,q}c_{i,q-1}d_q
=P_{i,q}(d_{q+1}c_{i,q}+c_{i,q-1}d_q)
=P_{i,q}(1-R_{i,q})=P_{i,q}-P_{i+1,q}.$$
Summing these equalities proves the claimed equality with $\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(P_{i,q}-P_{i+1,q})$.

proof.text:
For fixed $q$, induction on $k\leq r$ gives
$$\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}(P_{i,q}-P_{i+1,q})=P_{0,q}-P_{k,q}.$$
At $k=0$ both sides are zero; adding $P_{k,q}-P_{k+1,q}$ proves the next case by cancellation in the abelian group of homomorphisms. Take $k=r$ and use $P_{0,q}=1$ to finish the homotopy identity.

source.place: Paragraph (3); agent-written algebraic expansion of ordered-join calculations 5-6 in lem-sfb-ordered-join-partial-contraction. The blueprint itself does not state this auxiliary calculation.

proof.text:
Now fix a degree $q$ satisfying the support hypotheses, a proper subset $C\subsetneq I$, and $x\in A_{q,C}$. Choose $j\in I\setminus C$. Expanding the prefix recursion, with the stated order of application, gives
$$P_{r,q}(x)=(R_{0,q}\circ\cdots\circ R_{j-1,q})\bigl(R_{j,q}((R_{j+1,q}\circ\cdots\circ R_{r-1,q})(x))\bigr).$$
Empty composites are identities. Successively applying the preservation hypothesis shows that the inner argument of $R_{j,q}$ belongs to $A_{q,C}$. Hence $R_{j,q}$ kills it; every remaining homomorphism sends zero to zero. Thus $P_{r,q}$ kills every $A_{q,C}$. Express any $x\in A_q$ as a finite sum of elements of these subgroups. Additivity then gives $P_{r,q}(x)=0$, so $P_{r,q}=0$. No factors were commuted.
